Implementation of dt_format_to_regex:

def dt_format_to_regex(format_string):
    # mapping
    mapping = {
        '%Y': r'\d{4}',
        '%y': r'\d{2}',
        '%m': r'\d{2}',
        '%b': r'(Jan|Feb|Mar|Apr|May|Jun|Jul|Aug|Sep|Oct|Nov|Dec)',
        '%B': r'(January|February|March|April|May|June|July|August|September|October|November|December)',
        '%d': r'\d{2}',
        '%e': r'\d{1,2}',
        '%H': r'\d{2}',
        '%I': r'\d{2}',
        '%p': r'(AM|PM)',
        '%M': r'\d{2}',
        '%S': r'\d{2}',
        '%f': r'\d{1,6}',
        '%z': r'([+-]\d{4}|[+-]\d{2}:\d{2})',
        '%Z': r'\w+',
        '%c': r'.+',
        '%x': r'.+',
        '%X': r'.+',
        '%%': r'%',
    }
    # We need to escape regex special characters in literal parts.
    # Iterate over format_string and replace % directives with mapping, leaving other chars escaped.
    import re
    # Build regex pattern
    # Use re.escape for literal characters.
    # Use a loop over format_string.
    i = 0
    pattern_parts = []
    while i < len(format_string):
        if format_string[i] == '%':
            # handle %%
            if i+1 < len(format_string) and format_string[i+1] == '%':
                pattern_parts.append(re.escape('%'))
                i += 2
                continue
            directive = format_string[i:i+2]
            if directive in mapping:
                pattern_parts.append(mapping[directive])
            else:
                # unknown directive: escape it
                pattern_parts.append(re.escape(directive))
            i += 2
        else:
            # escape literal
            pattern_parts.append(re.escape(format_string[i]))
            i += 1
    return ''.join(pattern_parts)

But this simplistic mapping may not handle directives with optional length like %Y, but fine.

Also need to escape regex meta characters in literal parts.

Edge cases: format string may contain % followed by other char not in mapping. We escape it.

Also need to support timezone flexible: mapping for %z is above.

Ok.

Modify _to_group_name: replace '-' with '_' as well. And adjust collision logic accordingly.

Also update __all__ to include names.
